title: Grateful Dead Live at Seminole Indian Village on 1969-05-24
lineage: Cass > DAT >  DAT >  SONIC SOLUTIONS >  CD > CD > EAC [secure] > SHN

ai_review.summary: Pristine soundboard capture of a high‑energy May 24 1969 show with monster China Cat → The Eleven, blazing St. Stephen → Feedback and superb Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean, hiss‑free soundboard that lets the band’s 1969 fire shine through. Highlights include a thunderous China Cat > The Eleven segue, a fiery St. Stephen that erupts into feedback, and an unforgettable Lovelight/He Was a Friend of Mine stretch. Reviewers repeatedly note the show’s adventurous segues and relentless intensity.

ai_rating.rationale: Over twenty reviews, almost all 4‑5 stars, uniformly praise both performance and sound quality; the few minor complaints are about streaming glitches, not the music itself.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear mix with no hiss; reviewers call it “primo” and “pristine.” A few note occasional stream errors on "The Eleven" but the source itself is solid.

standout_songs: "He Was a Friend of Mine" (Friend of Mine)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Adventurous segues (China Cat → 11, Alligator → St. Stephen) keep the momentum high; a brief pause between drums and St. Stephen is noted but doesn’t hurt the overall flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for enthusiastic vocals (“Jerry slowly sing”) and overall excitement; his guitar tone described as “great Gar’s enthusiasm.”
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen highlighted on Alligator with “scratcher sounds” reminiscent of ’68, showing strong keyboard work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ/keyboard performance noted positively on Alligator and overall jam dexterity.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mention of a pause after the drums out of Alligator into St. Stephen; otherwise the rhythm section is praised for driving intensity.
